campbell.title: Campbell City Council — November 2, 2026
campbell.summary: The source for the November 2, 2026, Campbell City Council meeting is a video transcript, so this describes what the transcript shows was before the Council. The agenda centered on a proposal to replace the Campbell Technology Park office campus with a 290-home housing development (27 single-family homes and 263 townhome-style condos, 20% affordable). It also included a contract for police recruitment advertising and the consent calendar, with neighborhood speakers raising concerns about housing in single-family areas during open public comment.
keyTopics: Campbell Technology Park redevelopment: certify the environmental report, approve a planned development permit and vesting tentative subdivision map for 290 homes (27 detached homes, 263 townhome-style condos), remove 116 trees, and increase fence/wall height to 8 ft along Highway 17. Staff described it as a 'builder's remedy' project, meaning the city has limited ability to deny or reduce it under state housing law.

Traffic and safety for the housing project: staff reported no significant unavoidable impacts, with required pedestrian crosswalk upgrades near Campbell Technology Parkway and McGlincy Lane. Council members raised concerns about congestion, pedestrian/bike access, and the redwood trees along the Paseo de Palomas boundary.

Police recruitment contract: a one-year agreement with All Star Talent to run online recruiting and marketing for the police department, skipping the normal bidding process, funded from $175,000 in the 2026-27 budget.

Open public comment: residents of the White Oaks Manor neighborhood spoke about demolition of single-family homes for townhome projects and a proposed demolition control ordinance, and another speaker proposed fundraising for pedestrian safety measures.

Council announcements and consent calendar: reminders about the November 3 election and ballot deadlines, open board and commission vacancies, Veterans Day events, and consent calendar items 7.1 to 7.6.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — November 4, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the Saratoga City Council's November 4, 2026, meeting listed routine business items, a public hearing on a proposed temporary pause on certain detention-related facilities, and a proposed contract for an outside review of how the city is organized. Residents were also given time to speak on topics not on the agenda.
keyTopics: Public hearing on an urgent, temporary moratorium on establishing or operating detention or custodial detention facilities and custodial processing facilities while the city studies appropriate zoning and land use rules; the agenda proposes finding it exempt from CEQA under Guidelines section 15061(b)(3)
Proposed agreement with Bell Burnette & Atwater (BB&A) for an organizational assessment, at a cost of no more than $165,000 for fiscal year 2026-27

2026 Annual Code Update on the consent calendar, an ordinance amending many city code sections, including accessory dwelling units, urban lot splits, tree regulations, design review, density bonus and inclusionary housing rules, and housing on faith and higher education lands
Proposed revised Citywide Records Retention Schedule, listed on the consent calendar for adoption by resolution
Routine consent items: approving October 21 meeting minutes, accepting the October 22 accounts payable check registers, and accepting the Treasurer's Report for the month ended September 30, 2026

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026, Los Altos City Council meeting listed routine business such as purchasing city vehicles and awarding contracts for a park expansion and a Police Department backup generator. It also listed a proposed salary amendment for the City Manager, an extension of a temporary moratorium on certain detention and custodial facilities, and a presentation from Cal Water on water conservation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco for the Building B Park Expansion Project, not to exceed $166,225, with up to 10% in additional construction contingency.
The agenda listed a $417,400 contract with ELECCO of Milpitas to replace the Police Department's backup generator, with a construction contingency of up to 15%.

The agenda listed an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting an annual base salary of $375,000 effective July 5, 2026, plus an annual CPI/general salary adjustment provision starting July 2027.
The agenda listed an interim urgency ordinance extending Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium related to detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities.

The agenda listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures, a resolution on a Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of VTA, and a resolution to buy three replacement maintenance vehicles and one piece of equipment.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — November 17, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's published agenda for November 17, 2026, listed routine business such as approving meeting minutes and bills, along with items on zoning rule changes, a street maintenance project, and a possible new planning staff position. The agenda is a list of items before the Council, not a record of what was discussed or decided.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of minutes from the October 28, 2026, closed session and the November 2, 2026, special Town Council meeting.
An ordinance amending Chapter 29 (Zoning Regulations) of the Town Code was listed for adoption.
The agenda listed authorizing a Certificate of Acceptance and Notice of Completion for the 2026 Annual Curb project.
The Council was asked to consider adding a full-time Senior Planner position to the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget.
The agenda listed approval and ratification of the accounts payable check registers and payroll report.

san-jose.title: San José City Council — November 17, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, San José City Council meeting listed a mix of routine business, vendor contracts for city services, and event approvals. Items for consideration also included a proposed pause on approving data centers and other large energy-use projects, a legal settlement, and updates to the city's municipal code to comply with state law.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposed pause on approvals for data centers and large energy-use projects, along with developing urgency ordinances.
A settlement in the case Lopez et al v. City of San José, et al. was listed for consideration.

Several contracts and purchase orders for wastewater and utility operations were on the agenda, including HVAC improvements at the Regional Wastewater Facility, engineering services from Black & Veatch for pump station improvements, and a utility billing system upgrade with N. Harris Computer Corporation.
Non-exclusive franchise agreements for collecting and hauling residential clean-out material and construction and demolition debris were listed for consideration.

Event approvals were listed, including free use of City Hall plazas and the rotunda for the Tunnel of Terror event, free use of City Hall facilities for the Youth Empowerment Summit, and a World AIDS Day flag raising, quilt display, and lighting sponsored by Council Districts 9 and 3.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — November 17, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the Mountain View City Council's November 17, 2026, meeting listed a special session beginning at 5:00 p.m., followed by a long list of housing, zoning, parks, and infrastructure items. Several items concern two housing projects (749 West El Camino Real and 901-987 North Rengstorff Avenue) that were listed for potential settlement agreements and changes to their approvals, along with a broad update to residential zoning rules.
keyTopics: Potential settlement agreements and modifications to approval resolutions for a mixed-use project at 749 West El Camino Real and a housing project at 901-987 North Rengstorff Avenue (listed as a Builder's Remedy project)
R3 Zoning District Update, listed with adoption of R3 and R4 zoning text and map amendments, Precise Plan amendments, and General Plan land use and design changes
Updates to Chapter 41 of the City Code on park land dedication or in-lieu fees, including establishing a new Parks and Recreation Facilities Fee
Proposed code amendments restricting potable water irrigation of nonfunctional turfgrass and updating the recycled water service area

Ordinances on renting recreational vehicles for lodging in the public right-of-way and parking unhitched trailers in the public right-of-way, plus an extension of an interim urgency ordinance on detention or custodial facilities

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — November 17, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for Sunnyvale's November 17, 2026, City Council meeting listed a $3.27 million construction contract for the Plaza del Sol project, a proposed local emergency declaration tied to a developing El Niño, and two items on housing and parking for people living in vehicles. It also listed a below-market-rate housing fee ordinance and a salary and benefits change for the City Attorney.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a $3,268,600 contract with S & H Construction, Inc. for the Plaza del Sol Phase II rebid project, along with a 10% contingency ($326,860) and a $1,067,998 budget adjustment.
The agenda listed a resolution proclaiming a local emergency in Sunnyvale due to the developing 2026-2027 El Niño event.
The agenda listed a proposal to direct staff to prepare an implementation plan and environmental review for an interim housing community at 1240 Fair Oaks Way.
The agenda listed consideration of an RV permit parking program on Caribbean Drive and a study of a possible safe parking pilot program at 241 Commercial Street, with a $122,000 budget modification.
The agenda listed Ordinance No. 3263-26, which would change the city's below-market-rate ownership housing program rules on paying an in-lieu fee to meet the affordable housing requirement.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — November 17, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting listed a closed-door session with the City's attorneys about two existing lawsuits, a recognition of Small Business Saturday, and a consent calendar of routine items. The agenda also listed three discussion items: community funding and festival fee waivers, updates to the Council's procedures manual, and City Council compensation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a closed-session conference with legal counsel on two existing lawsuits against the City: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino and Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino, both in Santa Clara County Superior Court.
The agenda listed a recognition of Small Business Saturday, which falls on November 28, 2026.

The consent calendar listed routine items for a single vote, including adoption of a maximum rate schedule (Rate Period Seven) for Recology's recycling, organics, and solid waste services and adoption of the 2026 Emergency Operations Plan.
The agenda listed Council subcommittee recommendations on the Community Funding Policy and Festival Fee Waivers.
The agenda listed an ordinance amending Municipal Code Section 2.16.020 on City Council compensation, along with amendments to the Council Procedures Manual (previously postponed on May 5, 2026).

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — November 17, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed two meetings for Santa Clara's City Council on November 17, 2026: a 5:30 PM special meeting on Convention Center finances, followed by a 7:00 PM joint City Council/Stadium Authority Board meeting. The agenda listed a mix of routine business, a recognition for a local Little League team, and a housing project that the Council was asked to defer. The meeting was set up as a hybrid, with in-person attendance plus Zoom and phone access, and one councilmember planning to join remotely from Nashville.
keyTopics: The 5:30 PM special meeting listed an overview of Santa Clara Convention Center financial status reports for the fourth quarter of FY 2024/25 and all four quarters of FY 2025/26.

The agenda listed an action to defer consideration of a vesting tentative subdivision map and development agreement for a 590-unit residential and 15,000-square-foot commercial mixed-use project at 2610 El Camino Real, subject to SB 330 (2019). The agenda states the project is consistent with CEQA Guidelines Section 15183 and the General Plan land use.
The Council was scheduled to recognize the Santa Clara Westside Little League 11U All-Star Baseball Team for its 2026 season.

Routine financial items listed included the City bills and claims report for September 19 to October 19, 2026, and monthly financial status and investment reports for September 2026 with related budget amendments.

Residents could comment in writing through the eComment tab on the Council agenda page (closes 15 minutes before the meeting) or by emailing clerk@santaclaraca.gov by noon the day of the meeting; the agenda notes these comments are not read aloud.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — November 17, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine business such as the holiday closure schedule, the 2027 meeting calendar, and a set of contracts and labor agreements. Items before the Council included hiring temporary staffing firms, extending homeless outreach services, and approving new employee contracts through 2030.
keyTopics: Holiday closure schedule and winter recess: a resolution would set the city's holiday closures and let the City Manager or a designee sign project-related documents and handle urgent administrative items while the Council is on winter recess.
2027 meeting schedule: the Council was asked to approve its meeting calendar for 2027, with any changes requested at the meeting.

Temporary staffing and maintenance supplies: the agenda listed agreements with six firms for temporary staffing (up to $1.5 million total over five years) and with 74 vendors for citywide maintenance supplies, materials, and related services over five years.
Homeless outreach: an amendment to the city's contract with WeHope for outreach, assessment, and mobile hygiene services would add $163,522 to the contract.

Employee labor agreements: the Council was asked to consider successor agreements with the Milpitas Professional and Technical Group (ProTech) and the Mid-Management and Confidential Unit covering July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2030, along with a related FY2026-27 budget appropriation.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — November 16, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for the November 16, 2026, Palo Alto City Council meeting listed a joint study session with the Utilities Advisory Commission on the city's long-term water supply, along with items on housing, a creek bridge replacement, park improvements, and city employment agreements. It also included a closed-session item on potential litigation involving 156 North California Avenue.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a joint study session of the City Council and Utilities Advisory Commission on water-supply reliability, with presentations from city staff, the Bay Area Water Supply & Conservation Agency (BAWSCA), and the Yosemite Rivers Alliance, plus public comment.

The agenda listed a proposed zoning change for 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential to medium-density mixed use, to match the adjacent 2951 El Camino Real parcel and add the site to the city's housing inventory.

The agenda listed implementation of Housing Element Program 3.9(A), which aims to identify incentives at strategic locations to shift the economic benefit of redevelopment from commercial toward home building.

The agenda listed approval of an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Water District for $1,555,050 in local matching funds for the Newell Road/San Francisquito Creek Bridge replacement, and authorization to release a request for proposals for affordable housing at 340 Portage Avenue (Matadero Creek).

The agenda listed a park improvement ordinance for the Foothills Nature Preserve improvements, a Below Market Rate Housing Program audit follow-up report, and a colleagues' memo on zoning changes to enable permitting of childcare.
